title: An Introduction to Organic Certification
summary: A certifier explains the organic transition period, allowed substances, seeds and livestock rules for farmers seeking certification.

assertions.quote: it takes 36 months, 3 years, from the last application of a substance they consider prohibited
you need to provide pasture for ruminants, and you need to provide outdoor access for all animals
generally speaking, anything that is natural is allowed. Anything that is synthetic is prohibited. But there are a few exceptions

verdicts.note: Under 7 CFR 205.601 to 205.606, natural substances are allowed unless listed as prohibited, and synthetics are banned unless listed as allowed.

7 CFR 205.105 bars synthetic substances except those listed in 205.601/603 and bars nonsynthetic substances only where 205.602/604 prohibit them (e.g. arsenic, strychnine, rotenone), so natural is allowed and synthetic prohibited by default, with listed exceptions both ways.

assertions.quote: Once you're certified organic, you are required to use organic seeds.

verdicts.note: 7 CFR 205.204 requires organic seed, though non-organic untreated seed is allowed when organic seed is not commercially available.
7 CFR 205.204(a) requires organically grown seed and planting stock, but allows untreated nonorganic seed when an equivalent organic variety is not commercially available (never for edible sprouts).
